subject: Private backplane: translation squelch & temporary mitigation plan
messages:
From: Alex Chan <alex.chan@aurora-health.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Aurora NOC <noc@aurora-health.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Upload failures + truncated payloads after private cutover

Sergio,

We started validating data sync after the private deployment cutover this morning and are seeing repeated S3-like upload failures from our on-prem app stack. The client reports 502/connection reset during PUTs and multiple files show truncated payloads (partial object). The app team captured a packet capture and the pattern looks like MSS/fragmentation-related reassembly failures and several flows are returning via a different egress path (we see different source port translation on return).

Key notes from NOC:
- Errors started ~08:30 PDT after cutover to the new Clearbackplane VPC attachment.
- Problem affects 4 of 7 backend nodes; symptoms intermittent but reproducible on large multipart PUTs (>= 10MB).
- Packet capture attached (pcap excerpt).

We need immediate guidance — can you triage and propose a short-term mitigation so our nightly ingest doesn’t keep failing?

Thanks,
Alex Chan
Lead SRE, Aurora Health
Attachment: aurora-pcap-sample.txt
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Chan <alex.chan@aurora-health.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Upload failures + truncated payloads after private cutover

Marissa / Vanessa —

Looping you in. Initial read from Aurora’s pcap suggests two likely contributors: (1) asymmetric return path causing SNAT translation inconsistencies and (2) PMTU/MSS mismatch where large segments are being dropped/reassembled incorrectly. Aurora is using our private Clearbackplane attachment + customer edge; they reported the cutover to the new path this morning.

Can you validate routing policy for the Clearbackplane circuits (both Redwoven transit and customer on-prem) and confirm if any SNAT pools got exhausted / reused? If we need a hot mitigation I want options: temporary MSS clamp on the app-facing subnet, short-term expansion of ephemeral SNAT pool, and a conservative routing pin to force symmetric return.

I’ll reply to Alex with a calm heads-up while you triage.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Alex Chan <alex.chan@aurora-health.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Upload failures + truncated payloads after private cutover

Sergio / Alex —

Status from infra checks (quick runbook):
- Routing: Clearbackplane spoke advertised via our transit GW; I see two next-hops for return traffic — primary through rgw-us-west-2 (expected), secondary through partner-transit (unexpected). That explains the asymmetric return.
- SNAT: ephemeral port usage is high but not fully exhausted; however, return-path translation observed in pcap shows ports being rewritten inconsistently when return arrives via partner-transit.
- MTU: customer edge is set to 1500, but there are three intermediate devices (partner handoff + transit) that might be doing a 1460 clamp. I found multiple ICMP 'frag needed' messages in the capture but some were filtered on path.

Immediate mitigation I propose (low risk, reversible):
1) Increase ephemeral SNAT port allocation by 30% on the Clearbackplane NAT pool (adds headroom for parallel multipart sessions).
2) Apply an MSS clamp of 1400 on the app-facing subnet at the Clearbackplane attachment (prevents fragmentation on TCP transfers).
3) Add a temporary policy route on rgw-us-west-2 to prefer symmetric return through our transit for flows to Aurora's prefix (10.45.0.0/16) — TTL 24h and monitor.

If Aurora agrees, I can schedule 2) and 3) during the next 30 minutes (they’re configuration changes on our edge). 1) is a config change to NAT service and should be very quick as well.

I attached a short config diff and an excerpt of the pcap with the critical frames annotated.

Marissa Cole
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: clearbackplane-config-diff.txt
Attachment: aurora-pcap-sample.txt (annotated excerpt)
From: Alex Chan <alex.chan@aurora-health.com>

Cc: Aurora NOC <noc@aurora-health.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:27:00 -0700

Thanks for the quick analysis, Marissa.

We are comfortable with the staged approach. Two asks from our side before you make the changes:
- Can you confirm there will be no downtime to the app nodes during the NAT port increase and MSS clamp? We need to avoid breaking ongoing uploads.
- Please provide a rollback/playbook so our NOC can validate the change windows and watch the right metrics.

If you can apply the low-risk changes now we’ll run a validation job (small multipart PUT) from a couple of affected nodes and report back within 20 minutes.

—Alex
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chan <alex.chan@aurora-health.com>, Aurora NOC <noc@aurora-health.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Upload failures + truncated payloads after private cutover

Alex — quick update and plan (post-change):

What we did (15 Sep 2026 16:00 PDT):
- Increased ephemeral SNAT pool allocation for Clearbackplane by 30% (no restart required).
- Applied MSS clamp 1400 at Clearbackplane attachment for app-facing subnet.
- Installed a temporary policy route on rgw-us-west-2 to prefer symmetric return to Aurora prefix 10.45.0.0/16 (24h TTL).

Validation: Aurora NOC ran the multipart PUT smoke tests between 16:05–16:25 PDT. Results: 24/25 uploads completed successfully; the single failure was a client-side timeout that was retried and completed. Packet captures post-change show ICMP 'frag needed' messages reduced to near-zero and consistent port translation on return.

Next steps (recommended):
- Keep mitigation in place for 24 hours while we monitor: if stable, convert the policy route into a permanent symmetric-routing preference and document in the customer runbook.
- Extra: schedule a coordinated window with Aurora to run end-to-end traceroutes across the partner-transit path so we can identify and fix the intermediate device filtering ICMP.
- I attached a short playbook we used for the changes and the config diff pushed.

If Aurora wants, Vanessa and I can join a quick 30-minute postmortem tomorrow to capture action items and timeline for a permanent fix.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast collaboration.

—Sergio
